slides.text: The city's oldest apartment building had twelve floors, yet every resident insisted there had once been a thirteenth. The elevator buttons jumped from 12 straight to the rooftop. Blueprints showed no missing level. Old photographs didn't either. But every year, on the same rainy night, someone reported hearing children laughing from somewhere between the twelfth floor and the roof.

Curiosity got the better of me. On that night, I climbed the emergency stairs instead of taking the elevator. Halfway between the last landing and the rooftop, I found a door I'd never seen before. It opened into a brightly lit hallway where dozens of children played as though recess had never ended. They all stopped at once and stared at me.

A little girl walked over, smiling warmly. 'Did they finally remember us?' she asked. Before I could answer, someone called my name from the staircase behind me. I turned for only a second. The hallway was gone. So was the door. Back downstairs, an elderly resident looked at my pale face and quietly asked, 'How many children did you see?'
